concepts.definition: Binary search finds an item in a sorted list by checking the middle one and throwing away the half that cannot contain the target, then repeating on what is left.

unpacked.sorted list: items already in order, smallest to largest
unpacked.target: the value you are trying to find

workedExample.content: Find 7 in [1,3,5,7,9,11]. Middle is 5; 7>5 so drop the left half, leaving [7,9,11]. Middle is 9; 7<9 so drop the right half, leaving [7]. Found in 3 checks, not 6.

concepts.restatementPrompt: In your own words, why does checking the middle let you throw away half the list every single time?

gradings.followUpQuestion: What has to be true about the list for the half you discard to be safe to ignore?

activities.retrievalRole: learner draws the shrinking range as boxes and crosses out the discarded half at each step
activities.prompt: Draw the list as six boxes. Circle the middle, cross out the half that cannot hold 7, redraw what is left, and repeat until one box remains.

activities.retrievalRole: learner writes a punchline that only lands if each guess really does halve the space
activities.prompt: Make a POW! one-liner about a detective who always questions the middle suspect in the lineup first. Why is the detective so fast?
